records.name: Bicycle Coalition of Greater Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that pushes for safer streets for people who bike, walk and take transit in Philadelphia. Members and volunteers join advocacy walks, the Vision Zero work and community events.
records.what_you_do: Sign up on the volunteer page, join advocacy walks and street safety campaigns, and take part in youth cycling and bike events.

cost.text: Volunteering and advocacy events are free to join

first_step.how: Use the Volunteer link on the website, or call 215-242-9253
first_step.basis: The site invites anyone to volunteer and attend events, but the page does not say what a first shift looks like.

records.notes: The site lists a Vision Zero program, Families for Safe Streets and Transit Forward Philadelphia. The only event described is a Slow Down, Save Lives advocacy walk, but its year is not shown, so the status is probably_active rather than active. Email was not shown on the page.

records.name: Rev UP Philly
records.summary: A monthly open meeting for people working to make Philadelphia better for people with disabilities and seniors. Residents, workers and organizations come together online to plan change.
records.what_you_do: Join the monthly video meeting, share ideas, and sign up to help with disability and senior issues across the city.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on a Wednesday, 3:00 to 4:30 pm, held on Zoom

first_step.how: Fill in the short sign-up form linked on the Disability Pride PA calendar page, then join the Zoom meeting
first_step.basis: The page says the meeting is open to everyone interested in making change, and gives a clear sign-up form.

records.notes: Hosted under Disability Pride Pennsylvania. The newest listed meeting on the page is February 18, 2026, so later dates were not confirmed. Check the calendar for the current session. The page does not name a leader.

records.name: Tenant Union Representative Network (TURN)
records.summary: A Philadelphia tenant group that teaches renters their rights, runs eviction and repair clinics, and helps tenants form tenant unions in their buildings. It also staffs help lines for renters.
records.what_you_do: Attend a tenant rights workshop or clinic, call for counseling, or join the Network as a renter who organizes with neighbors.

cost.text: Counseling and hotline help are offered free to tenants. Landlord inspections and background checks cost a fee.

first_step.how: Call 267-635-4100 and press 3 for hotline help, or use the Join the Network link on the website
first_step.basis: The group explicitly serves tenants with no experience and says how to start: a hotline, workshops, and a join link.

records.notes: The group's own news posts are from 2022, but its services page is current and a Temple tenant resource page last updated June 19, 2026 lists it as a current tenant organization. The email shown on the page (info@celltechmd.com) does not match the group's domain, so it was left out. Address is from the group's own page.

records.name: William Way LGBT Community Center
records.summary: The LGBT community center in Center City. A core group of volunteers helps run its programs, from peer counseling and recovery meetings to the archives and library.
records.what_you_do: Staff the front desk, table at events, give tours, help with fundraisers, or join a regular shift or committee such as the arts committee or the archives.

first_step.how: Add your name to the Volunteer Mailing List for one-time roles, or email the committee you want to join
first_step.basis: One-time volunteer roles are open to anyone who signs up for the mailing list, and the page explains how to join regular shifts.

records.notes: The volunteer page is a working page with no dated items, so status is probably_active. The home page was not fetched. The 2018 Generocity list that names William Way also points to an older waygay.org URL, which now redirects to this site.

records.name: Mothers In Charge
records.summary: A Philadelphia violence prevention group that supports families who have lost someone to violence. It runs a monthly community breakfast, a welcome group for newly bereaved families, and a reentry dinner.
records.what_you_do: Come to the monthly community breakfast, join the welcome group for bereaved families, or ask about volunteering.

schedule.text: Community breakfast meeting on the first Saturday of each month, 11 am to 1 pm

first_step.how: Come to the first Saturday community breakfast, or RSVP to the welcome group by phone
first_step.basis: The page lists an open community breakfast and a welcome group for newly bereaved families, with a phone number to RSVP.

records.notes: The page lists a community breakfast on September 5, 2026, and a welcome group on October 20, 2026. The office suite is 301 in the text but 703 on the map link, so confirm the suite before visiting. The volunteer sign-up process is not described on the page.

records.name: Nationalities Service Center
records.summary: A more than 100-year-old group that helps immigrants and refugees in Greater Philadelphia with English classes, legal help, health services and youth programs. Volunteers help with classes, office work and events.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer as an English class tutor or assistant, help at the front desk, or help with events. The volunteer page lists the roles.

first_step.how: Look at the volunteer opportunities page at nscphila.org/how-help/volunteer-opportunities, then call 215-893-8400
first_step.basis: The group is open to the public and lists volunteer roles, but the page does not say what a first step looks like.

records.notes: The site lists Fall 2026 English classes and a news item dated August 13, 2026. The site does not list an email for volunteers, so none is recorded. The volunteer roles were named on the search snippet only, so verify them on the volunteer page.

records.name: JUNTOS
records.summary: A community-led group of Latine immigrants in South Philadelphia that fights for workers, parents, youth and immigrant families. It runs youth leadership, immigrant justice and community care programs.
records.what_you_do: Attend a volunteer orientation, help with community programs, or join the youth leadership program. The site also lists a volunteer link under Get Involved.

first_step.how: Use the Volunteer link under Get Involved, or call (215) 218-9079
first_step.basis: The group is open to the public and gives a way to contact them, but the page does not say what a first volunteer shift involves.

records.notes: The site has no dated 2026 items. Its events calendar was not fetched. A WHYY canvassing article about JUNTOS is dated November 2017, not 2026, so it was not used as evidence of current activity. A search snippet had claimed 2026 recruiting, but the article itself does not support that. Office hours are Monday to Friday, 10 am to 6 pm.

records.name: ACLU of Pennsylvania
records.summary: The state chapter of the American Civil Liberties Union. It fights for free speech, voting rights, immigrants' rights, LGBTQ equality and fair treatment in the justice system, and it has volunteer and chapter roles.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for the newsletter or the volunteer page, join a local chapter, or help with events and awareness work.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter or use the Volunteer link on the website
first_step.basis: The site says volunteer and chapter sign-up is open, but gives no detail on a first step.

records.notes: This is a statewide organization. The site has press releases dated July 1, July 22 and August 28, 2026. The Philadelphia chapter and its volunteer page were not confirmed, so check the Chapters page before treating it as a Philadelphia group. The address and phone are not on the fetched page.

records.name: Philadelphia Lawyers for Social Equity
records.summary: A nonprofit that gives free help to low-income Philadelphians clear old criminal records, so they can get jobs and housing. It also trains volunteers and hosts pardon help in neighborhoods.
records.what_you_do: Get trained as a volunteer in about 45 minutes, help people at a pardon hub, or invite the group to speak to your organization.

first_step.how: Call or email to book an appointment (walk-ins are not accepted during the move), or look at the Events page for a volunteer training
first_step.basis: Help is free and open to anyone who qualifies, and volunteers get a short training, but the site asks people to call ahead.

records.notes: The site is moving offices and says phones are temporarily out of service, so the listed phone number was left out. Email is the way to reach them during the move. The page's copyright year is not used as evidence. The 2026 status rests on the moving notice, which has no exact date.

notes: Searches used: 9 of 10. Fetches used: 25 (cap 60). Records written: 9 publish, 0 hide, 0 other verdicts. Lane G advocacy-rights returned fewer records than the 20 to 40 target because the search tool mostly returned directories, old listings and 2018 pages, and search budget ran out before more groups could be checked. The biggest gaps are: disability groups beyond Rev UP Philly, LGBTQ and women's rights groups (one center fetched; Equality Forum and Gay For Good still unchecked), worker groups (the city update named four groups; none has a confirmed website here), racial equity (NAACP branch site not located), and fetched leads that need their own sites checked next (Disability Rights PA, PICC, NSC and JUNTOS event calendars, VietLead, NDWA). Source text was not copied; summaries were written in our own words. Two search snippets had dates that the fetched pages did not support (a 2026 JUNTOS canvass, a Philly Goat Project item), and those were not used. Verdict counts: publish 9, hide 0, not_a_group 0, duplicate 0, out_of_area 0. Partisan check: no partisan groups were recorded. Philadelphia DSA was listed only as a lead, and it is a partisan socialist organization that should not be recorded as a group under the partisan rule. Mothers In Charge sign-up is by email or phone, and its breakfast is free.
